Carrie (CS): FYI Willow onboarding hitting intermittent SDK init slowdowns behind their corporate proxy. Seeing token refresh timeouts and a few 502/504s to api.redwood.ai. Sharing logs below, need triage.

Onboard-Bot: New onboarding ticket #WIL-422 created and linked to this thread. Assigned to Carrie.

Devon (Eng-Infra): thanks — can you paste the exact SDK version + a minimal log snippet? also are they using http proxy env vars (HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY) or a transparent proxy?

Carrie (CS): Node SDK v2.3.0, running in a lambda-like container inside their infra. They set HTTPS_PROXY to their corporate gateway. Log: ```[2026-03-20T14:02:11Z] token-refresh: attempt=1 error=\"upstream read timeout\" status=504 body=\"\"\n[2026-03-20T14:02:12Z] request: POST /v1/sessions status=504 duration=5200ms\n[2026-03-20T14:02:13Z] retrying... backoff=200ms```

Marta (Eng-Support): ok not obviously rate-limited. can you capture response headers from their requests? 504s + upstream read timeout often mean the proxy cut the backend connection.

Carrie (CS): got a sample response header from them: ```HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
Server: squid/4.13
X-Cache: MISS
X-RateLimit-Limit: 300
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 295
`
No 429s.```

Devon (Eng-Infra): Squid in the chain — that explains it. Common patterns: Squid has short read timeouts or mishandles chunked transfer from streaming endpoints. Two quick repro checks: 1) have them set NO_PROXY for api.redwood.ai and retry (bypass proxy), 2) curl the same endpoint through proxy with `-v` to compare timings.

Carrie (CS): they can't fully bypass corporate proxy for security policy, but they can run a curl test. I asked for `curl -v -x http://proxy:3128 -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/sessions`

Devon (Eng-Infra): also, try forcing HTTP/1.1 (`--http1.1`) in curl — some enterprise proxies handle HTTP/2->HTTP/1.1 translation poorly. If curl with proxy reproduces the 504 quickly, it's definitely proxy behavior.

Marta (Eng-Support): on the SDK side, we can make two quick mitigations without infra changes: bump init/connect timeout (default 5s -> 15s) and increase retry attempts with exponential backoff. Also add 504 to the transient-retry list (we typically retry 502/503/524).

Devon (Eng-Infra): agree. And recommend they enable connection keep-alive through the proxy and increase Squid's `read_timeout` if they control it. If they don't, ask their network team to check for chunked response handling and `reply_body_max_size`/`read_timeout` throttles.

Carrie (CS): customer ran curl with proxy and got: ```* Connected to proxy (10.10.0.5) port 3128 (#0)
> CONNECT api.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
*established TLS to api.redwood.ai
> POST /v1/sessions HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout
< Server: squid/4.13
* Connection #0 to host api.redwood.ai left intact
```

Devon (Eng-Infra): confirms proxy is terminating backend read. That reproduces it. Next steps: 1) we push a quick SDK patch to add 15s init timeout + 504 -> transient retry, 2) ask their network team to whitelist api.redwood.ai or tune Squid, 3) if they can, use an egress proxy that supports streaming or an allowlist so requests go direct.

Marta (Eng-Support): i'll prepare a short patch + rollout note for the Node SDK (v2.3.1) with configurable env vars: REDWOOD_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS and REDWOOD_TRANSIENT_STATUSES. We'll ship to them as a hotfix branch for validation.

Carrie (CS): I'll coordinate with their lead network engineer and schedule a 30m call. Will test hotfix first. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

Onboard-Bot: Linked PR #sdk-node-2.3.1-hotfix created.

Devon (Eng-Infra): one more tip for the call: ask them to capture proxy logs around the 504 timestamp (Squid access.log + cache.log) — that will show whether the proxy timed out waiting for the upstream.

Carrie (CS): noted. I'll follow up after the call with results. Closing for now, will reopen if hotfix fails. :white_check_mark:
